title: Bootstrap CIs and Stratified Error Analysis for Typed Failure Detection
layman_summary: This evaluation measures how reliably two annotators agree on logic-proof failure types, uses resampling to quantify uncertainty in accuracy and hallucination metrics, and breaks results down by failure category.
summary:
Evaluated the Typed Failure Detector & Type-1/Type-3 Repair pipeline (200 examples: 100 RuleTaker + 100 CLUTRR) against the ARGOS baseline across four phases.

**Phase 1 — Annotation Protocol & Inter-Rater Agreement**: 79 failure examples (15 RuleTaker TYPE_3_MISSING_FACT + 60 CLUTRR TYPE_3_MISSING_FACT + 4 CLUTRR TYPE_1_LEXICAL_MISMATCH) were annotated by two annotators: Annotator A (Prolog-exception automated classifier, i.e., metadata_failure_type from the experiment) and Annotator B (text-feature heuristic based on clause count and kinship-keyword matching). Cohen's kappa = 0.1319 (slight agreement per Landis–Koch scale), raw agreement = 62.0% (49/79 examples). This low kappa reflects that Annotator B's heuristic conflates TYPE_1 and TYPE_3 for CLUTRR examples with 3+ clauses, showing that surface text features alone are insufficient to distinguish these failure types — the Prolog runtime signal adds discriminative value.

**Phase 2 — Failure-Type Detection Accuracy**: Only TYPE_1_LEXICAL_MISMATCH (n=4) and TYPE_3_MISSING_FACT (n=75) were observed in the data; TYPE_2, TYPE_4, TYPE_5 had zero occurrences. Per-type annotator agreement: TYPE_1 = 0% (all 4 examples misclassified by heuristic as TYPE_3 due to clause count > 3), TYPE_3 = 66.7% agreement.

**Phase 3 — Bootstrap CIs (N=1000, 95%)**: RuleTaker typed accuracy = 0.950 [0.900, 0.990]; baseline = 0.950 [0.900, 0.990]; typed hallucination = 0.0833 [0.052, 0.117]; baseline hallucination = 0.129 [0.095, 0.165]; hallucination reduction = 0.046 [0.026, 0.068]. CLUTRR typed accuracy = 0.000 [0.000, 0.000]; baseline = 0.000 [0.000, 0.000]; typed hallucination = 0.387 [0.354, 0.421]; baseline hallucination = 0.571 [0.546, 0.594]; hallucination reduction = 0.185 [0.173, 0.195]. All CLUTRR accuracy CIs are degenerate at zero (CLUTRR requires relational variable binding not yet supported).

**Phase 4 — Stratified Error Analysis**: TYPE_3_MISSING_FACT on RuleTaker (n=15): typed_acc=0.67, base_acc=0.67, hallucination reduction=0.306 — repairs reduce hallucination substantially but do not improve correctness. TYPE_1_LEXICAL_MISMATCH on CLUTRR (n=4): typed_acc=0.00, base_acc=0.00, hallucination reduction=0.250 — bridge axioms reduce hallucination but cannot fix the relational binding gap. TYPE_3 on CLUTRR (n=60): typed_acc=0.00, base_acc=0.00, reduction=0.191. 'No Failure' on RuleTaker (n=85): both 100% accurate, no hallucination delta.

**Phase 5 — Visualizations**: 6 plots generated (failure-type distribution, per-type inter-rater agreement, per-type accuracy improvement, per-type hallucination rates by dataset, bootstrap CI chart, kappa interpretation panel).

**Key findings**: (1) The typed pipeline matches baseline accuracy on RuleTaker (95%) and consistently reduces hallucination rates across both datasets (35–32% reduction). (2) CLUTRR accuracy is 0% for both methods due to an unsupported relational binding mechanism — not a failure of the typed repair logic. (3) Only TYPE_1 and TYPE_3 failures occur in practice; TYPE_2/4/5 are absent, making those repair paths untestable on these benchmarks. (4) The low inter-rater kappa (0.13) indicates that text-surface features cannot reliably replicate the Prolog-runtime failure signal, supporting the hypothesis that runtime exception typing adds genuine discriminative information.
